panels.description: Wide, full page width. The Carnatic plain in the dry season, baked brown, with the wall of the Western Ghats rising behind it. A long column of cavalry winds toward a notch in the hills, its dust hanging in the air behind it. Bullock-drawn cannon at the tail. Hard white light. Distance only, no faces. The riders wear dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo or black turbans; no green anywhere on the riders, no red sashes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Before the Dutch became the enemy we watched from our beaches, there was another shadow that fell across Travancore each dry season.

panels.description: Insert, tight. A rider's ringed hand holding a rolled Persian letter inside a brocade silk kharita pouch, its drawstring closed with a lac seal. No writing visible anywhere, only the brocade and the seal.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It came with demands written in Persian and backed by Mughal seals that meant nothing in Delhi but everything to the men who carried them.

panels.description: Low angle. A commander on a fine horse at the top of a ridge, backlit by the sun so his face is lost in shadow: a heavy, bearded man in a white Mughal jama and a high turban of gold-shot cream silk with a jewelled aigrette, on a rich saddle cloth. He wears no red turban and no red sash. A banner bearer rides a length behind him with a plain dark banner, no device or lettering. The commander is looking south, away from us.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Chanda Sahib.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had heard the name in Pune, spoken with the wary respect one gives to a competent rival.

panels.description: Over the commander's shoulder, his cream turban and shoulder a dark silhouette in the near foreground. What he looks at: the green south opening out below the hills. Dense forested slopes and homestead gardens, pepper vines climbing jackfruit and areca trees, paddy on the valley floor, a river, and far off a port town with ships at anchor where the sea is a line of light. No terraces, no plantation rows.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had married into the Nawab of Arcot's family and climbed until he held Madurai in his fist.

panels.description: Narrow strip, full width. Marthanda Varma in his hall, standing straight, spear grounded at his side, looking directly out of the panel. Court dress: cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces, bare-chested. Unbowed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He saw what every ambitious man saw: pepper, ports, and a king who had not yet learned to bow.

panels.description: Wide. Evening. The steps of a small Kerala-style shrine among coconut palms: laterite base, sloping tiled roof, no gopuram. The sun is sinking behind the trunks. Ramayyan and Nagoji sit side by side on the steps, small in the frame. Ramayyan: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and stylus beside him. Nagoji in the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, talwar laid across his knees; clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, gold ear stud. His boots are off and set side by side on the ground below the bottom step; his feet are bare.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He came first in thirty-six. Before you washed up on our shore.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: We were weak, and Chanda Sahib knew it.

panels.description: Tight. Ramayyan's long fingers turning a small stone over and over.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: His cavalry came through Shenkottai pass like water through a cracked dam.

panels.description: Memory image, bleeding in at the panel edges rather than framed as a clean flashback. A village of thatched houses burning at dusk, seen from a distance. Horsemen are silhouettes against the flames. A family hurries away along a bund with bundles on their heads. No bodies, no blood.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: They burned villages. They took what they wanted.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: They sat on the edges of our kingdom and waited for the Maharaja to come with gold.

panels.description: Back on the steps, two-shot. Nagoji turned toward him. Ramayyan looking straight ahead, unashamed.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And he came?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He had no choice. We paid. Tribute, they called it. Protection money is what it was.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Fifty thousand rupees the first time.

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji in profile against the last of the sunset. Behind him, bleeding in like a stain: a dry Deccan field, a line of Maratha riders under a saffron swallow-tailed pennant at its edge, in white angarkhas and white pagdis with long bamboo lances, no red sashes, and a farmer standing in the stubble with his hoe, watching them. Nagoji himself is not in the memory.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of the Maratha sardars I had known, riding into Mughal country each dry season to collect chauth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We called it our right. The Mughals called it extortion. The farmers caught in between called it survival.

panels.description: Medium two-shot, the light going blue. Nagoji asking; Ramayyan still turning the stone.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: How many times?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Every year since. Sometimes Chanda Sahib himself. Sometimes his generals. Sometimes just the threat of them.

panels.description: Wide, almost silhouette: the two men on the shrine steps against the last light. Ramayyan's arm follows through as the stone arcs away into the gathering dark between the palms; Nagoji sits still beside him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Dutch watched all of it. They saw a king who had to buy his peace from one direction while they circled from another.

panels.description: Ramayyan pointing toward the southeastern hills, Nagoji following the line of his arm. The last light is a thin gold line along the ridge.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Every rupee we paid to Chanda Sahib was a rupee we could not spend on powder or walls.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: But we did build walls. At Aramboli. At the passes.

panels.description: Wide, bleeding in from the ridgeline: the Aramboli lines across the neck of a pass. A deep ditch, an earthen rampart topped by a timber palisade with firing loopholes, sharpened stakes, a timber gate. A few Nair sentries, tiny against the works: bare-headed with a front topknot, white mundu, matchlocks. Dusk. Leave generous sky for the balloons.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: The Maharaja understood that tribute buys time, not safety.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: I have seen them. From a distance.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: You will see them closer.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Ramayyan's face in the last light, a thin smile.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Walls cost less than tribute, in the long run. And they do not ride home when the rains come.

panels.description: Wide action. Near Nagercoil, where red-earth scrub and palmyra palms break into stream-cut, rocky ground at the foot of the hills. Nagoji, mounted, holds the mouth of a ravine with Dhanaji at his shoulder and a line of Nair musketmen kneeling among the rocks, matchlocks levelled; the Nairs are bare-headed with a front topknot, white mundu hitched for fighting. Dhanaji: stockier and broader than Nagoji, short trimmed beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic, no red sash, talwar drawn. Only Nagoji wears the rust-red turban and red sash. Out on the open scrub beyond, Chanda Sahib's riders in dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo or black turbans, no green, no red sashes, wheel away from the ravine mouth, faster, refusing the broken ground. Dust. No one falls.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Near Nagercoil.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We spoke of it afterward with the frustrated respect of men who had faced a worthy enemy.

panels.description: Afterward, late afternoon, in the same broken ground at the ravine mouth. Their horses blowing, heads down. Dhanaji (short trimmed beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no red sash) sits on a rock wiping sweat from his eyes; Nagoji stands holding both bridles. Dhanaji gestures at the rocks and gullies around them and the hills beyond.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Dhanaji admitted it.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: Their horse were better than ours. Faster on open ground. They knew the passes, knew the water holes.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: We did not fight them in the open. We let the land fight for us.

panels.description: High, wide view from the hills. A small walled town at the mouth of a pass, where the green slopes break into the flat brown plains beyond. A road runs through it and out the other side. No figures near the viewer. Leave open sky for the balloons, whose tails run off the panel edge.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had demanded Shenkottai. A dagger pointed at Travancore's belly.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And the Maharaja refused to give it up?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: He gave it up, then took it back, then gave it up again.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: Each time, men died. Each time, we paid in gold and blood.

panels.description: Night. Nagoji alone on the laterite parapet walk of a Travancore fort, looking northeast, his face lit from below by a clay oil lamp, an open wick dish, set on the parapet. Bleeding in above him across the stars: a column of Maratha horse under saffron swallow-tailed pennants, moving south, the riders in white angarkhas and white pagdis with long bamboo lances, no red sashes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: What I did not tell them was what I knew from my own people.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Raghuji Bhonsle's men were moving south. And Chanda Sahib, for all his cavalry and his Persian letters, was overextended.

panels.description: Full width. High and behind, from inside the fort. In the yard below the rampart, a lit doorway where Ramayyan (plain white cloth) and Dhanaji (white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic) stand talking, small, unaware. Above them on the rampart, Nagoji, seen from behind, pinches out the wick of the clay lamp. The parapet goes dark, and he stays facing the black horizon.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not know how the war would end. Men might think I was a spy, or worse, a lever they could use to bargain with powers I no longer served.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: So I kept my silence and watched the horizon for news.

panels.description: Wide. Dawn at the coastal camp: palm-thatched shelters, horse lines, the tiled roof of the war hall beyond. A lone rider comes in off the northeast road at a stumbling canter, his horse lathered white at chest and flank, trembling. He wears a plain cotton head cloth wrapped low and a dusty cream tunic and dhoti, no quilted coat. Nair guards in white mundu, bare-headed with a front topknot, carrying swords and round shields, run to catch the bridle.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Spring, 1741. The Dutch were tightening their grip on the coast.

panels.description: Insert, tight. The messenger's shaking hand holding out a single palm-leaf ola, bound with cord and sealed with a blob of wax. No writing visible.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had ridden through the night, through country that was still contested.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall: timber pillars, brass lamps on stands, a low table stacked with palm-leaf bundles and a brass tray of plain gold coins with no legible marks. Marthanda Varma seated on a low dais, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, his spear leaning against the dais at his right hand. Nair chieftains on either side: bare-headed with a front topknot (kudumi), white mundu and shoulder cloth, gold earrings, no turbans. Ramayyan standing near a lamp, breaking the wax. Nagoji standing apart at the back beside a pillar, the only man in the hall in a turban.
Tight. Ramayyan's hands on the leaf. His knuckles whiten; his fingers tighten on its edges. His face, at the top of the frame, has not changed at all.
Medium. Ramayyan lowering the leaf and turning to Varma, who sits on the dais at the edge of the frame. The whole hall still.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Chanda Sahib has fallen.

panels.description: Varma leaning forward from his seat. Ramayyan stepping up to hand him the leaf.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Fallen? Dead?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Captured. The Marathas took Tiruchirappalli. Raghuji Bhonsle's men have him in chains.

panels.description: Wide, from the front of the hall looking back. Every chief's head turned over his shoulder toward the back of the hall. The chiefs are Nair chieftains, bare-headed with a front topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, gold earrings, no turbans. Nagoji stands at the back by his pillar, the only turbaned man in the hall, and does not move.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They knew where I came from. They knew what the orange flag meant.

panels.description: Varma reading the leaf slowly, lips moving slightly. His expression gives nothing away.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Peshwa's war has done what our tribute could not.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Chanda Sahib will not ride south this season. Perhaps not ever.

panels.description: A local chief in the foreground (an older Nair chieftain, bare-headed with a front topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, heavy gold earrings) muttering sideways. Varma in the background, not troubling to look at him.

copy.speaker: CHIEF
copy.text: The Marathas will want payment for their service. They always do.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let them want. They are far away. The Dutch are close.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I will worry about debts when the creditors can reach my door.

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder in the foreground, looking straight down the hall. Nagoji small at the far end beside his pillar. The Nair chieftains between them (bare-headed, topknots, white mundu, no turbans) lean out of the line of the king's gaze.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You knew this was coming, Sawant?

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, stepping forward from the pillar. Measured.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I knew Raghuji Bhonsle was ambitious and that Chanda Sahib had made enemies.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But I did not know when or how the blow would fall.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have been here, Maharaja, not in Pune. My knowledge is old.

panels.description: Varma on the dais lowering the ola from the lamplight beside his seat, studying Nagoji over its edge for a long moment.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Old knowledge is still knowledge.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: What do the Marathas do with a captured Nawab?

panels.description: Nagoji at the low table, sure of himself now, setting one plain gold coin on a small stack from the brass tray as he speaks toward Varma, who is off-panel. Nair chieftains listening on either side, bare-headed, topknots, no turbans.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They will hold him. He is worth more alive than dead.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The Marathas are patient. They will extract every pagoda they can before they let him go.

panels.description: Three-shot, with the open side of the hall and the sea showing beyond them. Varma on the dais hands the ola back; Ramayyan, beside the dais, takes it and tucks it into the fold of his white cloth; Nagoji at the edge of the frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And while they extract?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: While they extract, he cannot ride south.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then we have a window. The Marathas have given us a gift, whether they meant to or not.

panels.description: Wide, full width. Varma rising, spear in hand, the Nair chieftains (bare-headed, topknots, white mundu, no turbans) getting to their feet around him. He has already turned toward the open side of the hall and the sea beyond it.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Enough talk of Arcot. The Dutch are the enemy in front of us.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let the Marathas deal with the shadow at our back. We have our own war to win.

panels.description: Wide. Night in the camp, cookfires and low talk: Nair soldiers (bare-headed, topknots, white mundu) and a few Deccan riders in white pagdis sit at the fires. Nagoji walks alone between the groups. One old Nair soldier nods to him as he passes; beside that man another Nair watches him go with narrowed eyes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: As if my people's victory was somehow mine.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Others wondered what other secrets I kept behind my Maratha face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now that shadow had been lifted by men I no longer served, men who would not even know my name if I returned to Pune.

panels.description: Nagoji on a low rise above the coast, seen from behind. The sea is black; the Dutch ships cannot be seen. Wind moves the tail of his turban.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had fled the Peshwa's justice. I had washed up on this foreign shore with nothing but the scars on my back and the skills in my hands.

panels.description: Vision only, bleeding across the night sky above the sea; the figure on the rise is not in this panel. Somewhere in the Carnatic, a captive of rank seated in a tent: a heavy, bearded man in a soiled white Mughal jama and a high cream turban with its jewel gone, his face in shadow, iron at his wrists. Maratha officers in white angarkhas and white or saffron pagdis, no red sashes, count coin on a cloth before him. A saffron swallow-tailed pennant hangs at the tent door.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And now, without knowing it, the very power I had escaped had done more to secure Travancore's eastern frontier than all my drills and all my riding.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The world turns strangely. One man's capture becomes another man's freedom.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face in the sea wind, campfire smoke drifting across it. Not triumphant. Certain.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Tomorrow, or the day after, the Dutch would land at Colachel, thinking they faced a king still bleeding from two fronts.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were wrong.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji has turned from the sea and is walking back toward the fires of the camp. Below the rise, the long pale beach runs away into the dark, empty, waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The shadow from Arcot had lifted. Now there was only the sea, and the enemy upon it, and the sand where we would meet them.

frames.review_note: Clean. Dry Carnatic plain with rocky hills and a notch, the column winds toward it through dust, bullock-drawn cannon at the near tail, riders in dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo turbans, plain cream banners, no green, no red sashes, no faces. Very minor: one tiny distant banner near the notch has a few dark specks, unreadable at print size. Wide clear sky across the top for the caption. All checks pass (no text, no anachronism, no gore).

All hard checks pass on v02. There is no Nagoji, Kayal or Varma in this insert, so the ear, chin, footwear and horse checks do not apply. The seal is plain lac with no impression and there is no text or pseudo-text anywhere. The setting is the dry Carnatic plain, not Kerala. The background riders wear dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo turbans, with bullock-drawn cannon, which matches panel 1.1. The ringed hand is anatomically sound. A large clear blue sky across the top third leaves room for the caption. Minor, not disqualifying: the pouch reads as a closed brocade bag, so the rolled letter is implied rather than seen, and the framing is slightly less tight than an insert. v01 is rejected because its wax seal carries an impressed pseudo-script pattern (text in the art). Its background riders also wear white turbans and ochre or orange sleeves, with a red saddle cloth at the bottom, which breaks continuity with panel 1.1.

Acceptable. The commander is on a dark horse at the ridge top with the sun behind him: heavy build, beard edge only, white jama, gold-shot cream high turban with a plumed jewelled aigrette, rich saddle cloth, no red. He faces away down the valley, so his face cannot be read. The banner bearer rides behind with a plain dark banner. Riders wear quilted coats and dark turbans, and bullock-drawn cannon are in the column below, consistent with 1.1. Horse anatomy is sound. Large clear sky at upper right takes both captions. The face entry marks the back of the commander's head, the key subject the captions should avoid, not a readable face. No text, gore or anachronism.

Acceptable with minor notes. The view south matches the script: forested Ghats slopes, pepper vines climbing a jackfruit tree, coconut and areca, flat paddy, a river, and a distant port with square-rigged ships at anchor on a glittering sea line. No terraces, no plantation rows. The commander is seen only from behind, beard edge but no readable face, and the quilted, dark-turbaned riders at left match 1.3. Minor issues: (1) the turban is plain cream with no visible gold-shot band or aigrette, and the jama has a plain sash, a slight costume drift from 1.3; (2) the near figure is lit and large rather than a dark silhouette; (3) the distant port has a few spires and towers, plausible for a 1730s Malabar port with European churches and a fort. Clear sky at top centre takes the caption. The face entry marks the back of the commander's head. No text, gore or anachronism.

Clean. Varma matches the varma-v1 sheet: face, curled moustache, red forehead mark, pearl earrings, cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, gold necklaces and armlets, cream-and-gold cloth. This is the chapter 12 pages 1 to 4 formal court look, with no side knot or headband. He stands straight, gazes directly out, and holds the spear upright at his side; the butt runs off the bottom edge. Hands are sound. The Travancore hall has timber pillars, laterite bases, a tiled roof and brass nilavilakku lamps with open wicks, no throne and no audience. Clear sky between the right pillars and Varma, upper right of centre, takes the caption without covering him. No text, gore or anachronism.

All hard checks pass on v02. Nagoji's ear has a tiny flush stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it (it is pale gold, close to pearl, but reads as a small stud). His chin is clean-shaven, the moustache is thick and curled, his sleeves are down to the wrists, and the talwar lies across his knees. He is barefoot, with his brown boots side by side on the ground below the bottom step. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, stylus in hand, palm-leaf bundle on the step beside him. The seating is now Nagoji left and Ramayyan right, which matches 2.4. The shrine has laterite steps, a sloping tiled roof and open-wick brass lamps, with no gopuram, and the sun sets behind the palms. There is no text, no anachronism, and the hands are sound. The sunset sky at upper left and upper centre gives room for both of Ramayyan's balloons. Minor points: (1) the figures fill more of the frame than 'small in the frame' asks; (2) a tiny ink curl sits on Ramayyan's bald scalp near the hairline, reading as a stray hair wisp; (3) the boots have stitched welts and heel pull-tabs, so they look slightly like modern work boots, though they match the sheet's laced brown boots; (4) the talwar pommel is a curled hook rather than a disc. v01 is not acceptable because its ear has a hanging gold drop, and its seating is mirrored against 2.4.

Minor only. Ramayyan's hair is swept back rather than the curly side-halo on his sheet, and he has light stubble, but he reads clearly as Ramayyan: thin, sharp features, receding hairline, plain white cloth. The wall behind is whitewashed while 2.1 has laterite walls (the steps are still laterite). The palm-leaf bundle reads a little like a bundle of sticks. The hands are anatomically sound and turning the stone (the beat). There is no text, and the sky top-right and the white wall top-centre leave clear space for the balloon.

Clean against all hard checks. The memory image bleeds in at the edges, as the script asks. Thatched village burning at dusk, rider silhouettes against the flames, a family on a bund carrying bundles on their heads, no bodies or blood, a plain unlettered dark banner. Minor notes: the woman wears a red short-sleeved blouse, and a tiny crossed roof pole on the right-hand hut reads as roof timber at print size. Clear sky top-left and smoke top-centre take both off-panel lines. Tails point to the left frame edge, toward Ramayyan in 2.2.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, his chin is clean-shaven, he is barefoot with sleeves down, and he holds the talwar across his lap. The beat is right: Nagoji turned toward Ramayyan, Ramayyan looking ahead. Hands are sound and there is no text. Continuity issues: (1) the steps and pillars are grey granite, but the script and 2.1/2.2 have red-brown laterite; (2) the seating is mirrored against the current 2.1 (Nagoji screen-left here). The 2.1 correction asks for this order, so 2.1 will follow 2.4. (3) The boots stand on a lower step rather than on the ground below the bottom step (minor). Ramayyan's two lines fit in the sunset sky upper right. Nagoji's short line has to sit top-left, over the shrine doorway or the roof band. That space is adequate but busier, and it covers no faces.

v03 is acceptable and is the only version that passes the hard checks. The regenerated ear is a small gold stud flush on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. He has a thick curled moustache, sits barefoot on the laterite shrine steps with his boots together below him, and his sleeves are down. He wears the rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash. The Deccan memory bleeds in from the left as the script asks: a plain saffron swallow-tailed pennant, riders in white angarkhas and pagdis with lances and no red sashes, and a farmer with his hoe in the stubble. There is no text and nothing anachronistic, and the setting matches the 2.1 shrine at sunset. The sky at top left and centre is open, low-detail space for both captions. Two small faults remain for the author: faint stubble texture on the jaw and chin (light, reads as shading at print size), and a scabbarded curved sword with a sabre-style knuckle-guard hilt rather than a disc-pommel talwar, though the blade itself is curved. v01 and v02 both fail the ear check because they show hanging gold drop earrings. They also have heavier stubble, v01 and v02 give the farmer a spade instead of a hoe, and v02's sword is nearly straight, so neither works as a backup.

Passes the hard checks. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, sleeves down, barefoot, boots set together on the step, talwar across his lap. The blue-going light and the shrine match the script beat. Minor: Ramayyan's stone is fist-sized and grey, larger than the small dark stone in 2.2. He also touches it with the stylus as if carving it rather than simply turning it. Neither is disqualifying. Balloon space: open sky upper left for Nagoji, and the roof and sky band upper right for Ramayyan's long line.

v02 passes every hard check. Nagoji: small flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, red sash, sleeves down, barefoot, talwar across his knees, boots set side by side on the step below. Ramayyan matches his sheet and his arm follows through as the stone arcs toward the palms. The setting is a laterite Kerala shrine with palms at last light, almost silhouetted. No text or anachronism, and the upper-left sky is open for the balloon. Two minor notes. The warm orange sunset is a little warmer than the blue dusk of 3.1. The boots sit on the step just below his feet rather than at the foot of the stair. v01 is rejected: Nagoji throws the stone while Ramayyan writes, which reverses the script beat.

v02 passes every hard check. Nagoji: tiny flush gold stud, clean-shaven chin with only light shading, moustache, turban, sash, sleeves down, barefoot, talwar across his knees, boots together on the lower step. Ramayyan points toward the hills, and Nagoji follows the line of his arm. A thin gold line of last light runs along the ridge. The setting is the same laterite shrine with lamps, consistent with 3.1. No text or anachronism. The upper-right sky is open for both balloons. One minor note: the talwar reads as a bare blade or a brass-edged scabbard, where 3.1 shows it sheathed. v01 is rejected: Nagoji does the pointing and Ramayyan writes, which reverses the beat. v01 is also a warm, bright sunset rather than the blue dusk.

Shows the script beat: the Aramboli lines across the neck of a pass at dusk. It has a deep ditch, an earthen rampart, a timber palisade with loopholes, sharpened stakes and a timber gate. The few tiny Nair sentries are bare-chested and bare-headed with topknots, wearing white mundu and carrying matchlocks. The sky is generous and the torches are open flame. No text, no anachronism. Minor notes: (1) three plain off-white pennants fly on the works and could read as white flags rather than a Travancore standard (silver conch on red); they are not lettered, and the upper-left one may be partly covered by balloons. (2) The topknots sit on the crown more than the front, which can't be seen at this size. (3) The frame is a clean wide shot; the bleed from the ridgeline is a layout matter. The speakers are off-panel on the shrine steps, so the tails go to the side edges: Ramayyan to the right, Nagoji to the left, matching their seating in 3.1.

Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin face, receding hairline with curly black hair at the sides and back, a faint cheek mark, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. The thin, knowing smile is the beat. The hands holding the stylus and bundle are sound. There is wide, low-detail sunset sky on the right for the long balloon. No text or anachronism. Minor: the sun is still a sliver above the horizon, so the light is a little warmer and earlier than the blue dusk of 3.1. That is acceptable as 'last light'.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

v02 passes every hard check: a small gold stud sits on the earlobe with nothing hanging below it; clean-shaven chin; both of Nagoji's sleeves are down to the wrists; boots; talwar at the sash; rust-red turban and red sash. Both horses are solid bays with black manes and lower legs and no white on any face or leg. Nagoji stands holding both sets of reins while the horses blow with their heads down. Dhanaji matches his sheet (short beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash, slip-on shoes) and sits on a rock wiping sweat from his eyes with a cloth. The setting is the same red-earth broken ground with gullies, a stream, palmyras and hills in late-afternoon light, and it matches 4.1. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Minor: the ear stud is a little oval. Dhanaji's open palm, swept out to the right, hovers just above the near horse's forelock, so it reads partly as a gesture toward the horse rather than plainly at the gullies and hills, though it still points toward the landscape at right. Lettering space: clear sky at upper centre-left above Dhanaji (about x 0.22 to 0.40) and across the upper right (x 0.55 to 1.0) holds the caption and both Dhanaji balloons without covering a face or hand. v01 still fails: rolled sleeves with bare forearms, and white face markings on both horses.

Minor only: the town's two-storey whitewashed houses with red tiles look a little Iberian, and a white tower with a pitched cap near the centre could read as a bell tower. A temple gopuram and the walled gate keep it reading as a South Indian frontier town. Otherwise clean: a high, wide view from the hills of a small walled town at the mouth of a pass, green slopes breaking into the flat plain beyond, and a road through the gate and out the other side. There are no figures, no text and no anachronism, and a large open sky across the top holds the caption and three off-panel balloons, whose tails run off the left (Nagoji) and right (Ramayyan) edges.

Minor only: the ear stud is a slightly large gold bead but sits flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. There is faint stipple shading along the jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. His face is lit more by the night sky than from below by the lamp. Everything else passes: rust-red turban, cream tunic with the sleeve down to the wrist, red sash and talwar; a laterite parapet; a clay open-wick dish lamp (no glass); the vision column carries saffron swallow-tailed pennants, with riders in white angarkhas and white pagdis with long lances and no red sashes; no text. The starry sky at upper left holds both captions clear of the face and the column.

Minor: (1) A plain white flag flies on the far tower at top right. It is not the Travancore conch-on-red standard and could read as a surrender flag, so the letterer should place the second caption over it or it should be retouched. (2) Nagoji's turban has a long tail hanging down his back that the sheet does not show. Everything else passes. The view is high and behind, inside the same laterite fort as 4.4. Nagoji, seen from behind, pinches out the clay lamp's wick and a thread of smoke rises. His sleeve is down to the wrist, his gold ear stud is flush on the lobe and his chin is clean. In the lit doorway below, Ramayyan (receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle, barefoot) and Dhanaji (beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, talwar) talk, small and unaware. There is no text. The dark sky and treeline band along the top holds both captions.

Acceptable. Minor notes only: the sun sits on the sea horizon, but a dawn sun cannot rise over the sea on the west-facing Travancore coast. Readers may take it for dusk, and no lettering says dawn. The courier's head cloth is wrapped a little higher than 'low', but it is plain and distinct from Nagoji. The lather on the horse reads partly as a dappled coat. The background flag is plain white with no text. The beat is there: a bearded courier in a dusty cream tunic and dhoti on a lathered, stumbling horse; bare-headed Nair guards in white mundu with topknots, swords and round shields run to catch the bridle; horse lines, palm-thatch shelters and the tiled war hall behind. No text, no anachronism, hands and horse legs sound. Clear sky at top centre for the caption.

Acceptable. Minor: the light is full morning daylight, brighter than the dawn in 5.1, and the shaking of the hand is not conveyed. The ola is a thin flat stack of palm leaves bound with cord, with a dark-red wax blob. The seal's impression is a blurred texture with no legible letters. The hand is anatomically sound and the courier's cream sleeve and brown waist cloth match 5.1. Clear sky at upper right for the caption.

Accepted on the last attempt with one fault left. In v03, Nagoji's ear has a small flush gold stud, but a tiny round gold ring still hangs just below it on the lobe. It is about 10 px across and barely visible at print size. Otherwise v03 is identical to v02 and passes the hard checks. Nagoji is in the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, cream trousers and boots. His chin is clean-shaven and he stands apart by a pillar at the back. Varma is in the page-5 war-hall look: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, bare chest, cream-and-gold mundu, gold necklaces and the spear at his right hand. Ramayyan matches his sheet and is breaking the wax seal on the ola. The palm-leaf bundles and the tray of plain gold coins carry no marks. There is no text, gore or anachronism. Smaller deviations, left as they are: Varma sits on a carved chair on a red-carpeted platform rather than a plain low dais. The chieftains wear their knots on the crown, not a front kudumi. Nagoji's talwar scabbard is only slightly curved, but it matches the commander sheet. The panel has no lettering, so it needs no balloon space. v02 is the same composition with a clearly visible bell-shaped drop earring, so it is a weaker backup. v01 fails the beat: Ramayyan is writing with a stylus instead of breaking the wax, a map is added to the table and Varma's hair is loose. v01 also has a drop earring.

Acceptable. Minor notes: the ola he grips is a thicker cord-bound bundle than the thin sealed strip in 5.2, and no broken wax shows. He appears seated at a table, while he stands in 5.3 and 5.5. The framing is medium-close rather than tight on the hands. The beat reads: big tense hands with knuckles hard on the bundle under a composed, unmoving face at the top of the frame. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin face, receding hairline, curly sides, plain white cloth). The setting matches the hall: brass lamps, white plain flags, sea through the pillars, plain coin tray. The blank leaf and stylus on the table carry no marks. Hands are sound. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable with notes. Ramayyan still holds a stylus over his palm-leaf bundle, as if mid-note, rather than lowering the opened ola, but he is turned to Varma with the leaf held low, and the bundle and stylus are his sheet props. Varma's knot sits high at the back-left of the crown rather than squarely above the left ear: close enough to the war-hall look, and he is bare-headed with no turban, crest or headband, bare-chested, in a cream mundu with gold border and gold necklaces. He has slight jaw shadow. His spear stands behind his carved chair by the dais. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The hall, lamps, coin tray, seated bare-headed Nair chiefs, the guard and the sea view are consistent with 5.3 and 5.4, and the hall is still. No text, hands sound. Clear sky between Ramayyan's head and the centre pillar, with the roof above it, gives room for the short Ramayyan balloon.

All hard checks pass. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth) and steps forward offering the leaf; Varma is in the page-5-onward war-hall look (bare head, hair knotted at the back on his visible left side, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces, spear standing by the dais) and leans forward reaching for it. Hands are sound. Same open coastal hall, lamps and table as pages 5 and 6. No text. Minor only: the ola is drawn as a small corded bundle rather than a single leaf; background chiefs wear loose hair and beards rather than clear front topknots, and one small background figure has a pale head cloth; the coins on the tray read silver rather than gold. Lettering room: open sky above Varma for VARMA; the roof and rafters above centre-left for RAMAYYAN's longer line.

All hard checks pass. This is a wide shot from the front of the hall looking back, with chiefs in white mundu and shoulder cloths, topknots, gold earrings and no turbans. Nagoji stands still at the far end in front of a pillar, the only turbaned man. Nagoji is in the commander look: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, sleeves down, boots, talwar. The banners are plain cloth and nothing in the art is text. Minor: the two nearest left-hand chiefs face the camera and glance sideways instead of turning over their shoulders toward the back, though all the other chiefs do turn back. Topknots sit at the crown rather than the front, and the coins on the foreground tray read silver. The caption fits over the roof and rafter band at the top left, or the open sky above Nagoji.

All hard checks pass. Varma matches varma-v1 in the war-hall look: bare head, knot above his left ear, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces. He sits on the dais reading the leaf with lips slightly parted and a closed, neutral expression. Both hands are sound. Same hall, coin tray and lamps. Minor: the leaf face carries faint, broken grain-like dashes that only hint at writing lines. They have no letter shapes and read as leaf grain at print size, so the leaf could optionally be retouched blank. The spear stands at his left side (frame right), not at his right hand. Lettering room: open sky to the right of his head (between the spear and the right pillar) and above his head under the roof.

All hard checks pass. The foreground chief is an older Nair chieftain (grey hair in a topknot, heavy gold earrings, white mundu and shoulder cloth) muttering sideways to the man beside him. His hand on his chest is sound. Varma stands in the background on the dais in the war-hall look (bare head, knot, bare chest, cream-and-gold mundu, necklaces), with the spear in his right hand, looking away and not at the chief. Standing with the spear fits the 'carried when he rises' rule and matches 6.5, where he also stands with it. Minor: a few grey streaks in Varma's hair (6.1 and 6.3 show it black); the small paper map on the table has tiny illegible scribble marks that read as map detail, not letters, at print size. Lettering room: the roof and palm area at top left for CHIEF, and the open sky between the centre pillar and Varma for his two lines.

All hard checks pass. The camera looks over Varma's bare shoulder: profile edge, moustache, knot on top, gold necklaces, spear in his right hand, matching 6.4. It looks straight down the hall to Nagoji, standing small at the far end by a pillar, with the chiefs on both sides leaning out of the king's line of sight. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold studs with nothing visibly hanging, sleeves down to the wrists, red sash, talwar and boots. Banners are plain. Minor: Varma's hair falls as a loose curly mass with a crown knot and a little grey, rather than a neat side knot. The coins on the tray read silver, while 6.4 shows gold. The paper map has tiny illegible scribble marks, unreadable at print size. Lettering room: the roof and rafter band at top centre, or the sky and palms left of the centre pillar, clear of Nagoji's head.

v02 passes every hard check. Ear: a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging (checked at 3x zoom). Chin: clean-shaven, with thick curled moustache, strong cheekbones and straight nose, matching nagoji-v2. Costume: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, talwar hilt at the sash. Footwear is out of frame (waist-up close-up), so there is no boot conflict. It is now a true close-up: he advances past the dark timber pillar and turns three-quarter to frame right, toward the off-panel dais, which matches Varma looking frame left in 7.2. Setting matches 6.x and 7.3/7.4: the open side of the hall with sea, palms, brass lamps, the coin tray and leaf bundles on the low table, bare-headed topknotted Nair chiefs in the background. The banner is plain red cloth. No text or anachronism. Minor: a faint stipple of skin texture on the cheek and jaw that reads as shading, not stubble or beard. Lettering: a large clear sky area right of his face (roughly x 0.5 to 0.95, y 0.08 to 0.55) holds all three balloons without covering a face. v01 still fails: a hanging gold drop earring, and a full-length wide shot instead of a close-up.

v02 passes the hard checks. Varma matches varma-v1: moustache, Vaishnavite namam, pearl earrings. He is in the page 5+ war-hall look: bare head, jet-black hair with no grey (checked at 3x), knot at the back-left of the head behind the visible LEFT ear, no turban, crest or headband, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces. He sits on the cushioned dais between brass lamps. The single sealed palm leaf is lowered to chest height, and his eyes are lifted over it toward frame left (the off-panel Nagoji), which fits the beat and the screen direction of 7.1. Both hands are sound. The setting matches the page: the open side of the hall to the sea, the coin tray and leaf bundles on the low table. No text on the leaf, no anachronism. Minor: the grounded spear stands at frame right, by his left side rather than his right hand, as already accepted in 6.3. A plain blue hanging cloth shows at the right edge where 7.1 has a red one. His pearl drop earrings differ from the gold balls in 7.4/7.5. Lettering: clear sky between the left pillars (about x 0.17 to 0.45, y 0.12 to 0.5), left of his face, for both balloons. v01 fails on clear grey and silver streaks in his hair.

Clean on every hard check. Ear: tiny flush gold stud, nothing hanging. Chin: clean-shaven, with only light jaw shading. Rust-red turban, sleeves down, sash and talwar. Seated cross-legged with his feet hidden behind the table, so footwear is not in view. He sets one gold coin on a small stack beside the brass tray and looks up to frame right toward the off-panel Varma. Topknotted, bare-headed Nair chieftains and guards sit and stand on either side. The setting matches the page: open side to the sea with ships, timber pillars, brass lamps. No text. Large plain wall in the upper centre-right for both balloons. Minor: the coin carries a faint embossed design (not lettering), and an unoccupied raised platform with a weapon rack stands in the background.

Hard checks pass. Nagoji at the left edge: tiny flush gold stud, clean-shaven chin, boots, sleeves down, rust-red turban, sash and talwar. Varma: bare-headed with black hair in a knot, no turban or crest, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces, spear by the dais. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, white cloth. The open side of the hall with the sea and ships shows behind them. No text. Wide clear sky between Ramayyan and Varma for the three balloons. Minor continuity slip: Varma still holds out a bundle while Ramayyan, with his stylus, tucks a second bundle into the fold of his cloth, so the ola reads as doubled; it is also drawn as a bundle rather than the single leaf of 7.2. The handoff gesture still reads clearly.

v02 passes the hard checks. It is a wide 3:1 strip (2172x724). Varma stands on the low dais in the war-hall look: bare head, hair black (only dark blue-grey sheen highlights, no silver streaks like v01, checked at 8x), knot at the back of the crown, no turban or crest, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces and armlets. The spear is upright in his RIGHT hand. Bare-headed, topknotted Nair chieftains in white mundu push up from their mats around him and turn toward the open side. The open side of the hall shows the sea, ships with tiny plain pennants and a stone coastal fort. Brass lamps, timber pillars and a tiled roof match 7.1 to 7.4. Hands and anatomy are sound, and there is no text or anachronism. Minor: his body still faces the camera with only his head turned toward the right-hand opening and the fort, so 'already turned toward the sea' reads only partly (v01 had the same pose). The knot sits at the back of the crown rather than above the LEFT ear, consistent with 7.4. His forehead mark is a small dot where 7.2 shows the U namam. Lettering: clear sky between the centre pillars over the sea (about x 0.5 to 0.7, y 0.17 to 0.42), right of his head, for both balloons, clear of faces and ships.

v01 fails: Nagoji's ear carries a hanging gold drop. v02 (ear region edit) passes: a round gold stud sits flush on the lobe with nothing hanging, the seam is clean, the chin is clean-shaven with a thick curled moustache, sleeves are down, he wears boots and a talwar, and the commander colours are right. The beat reads: a night camp with cookfires, bare-headed Nair soldiers with topknots in white mundu, and white-turbaned Deccan riders. Nagoji walks alone between the groups while an old grey-haired Nair looks up at him and a second Nair watches with narrowed eyes, though from across the path rather than right beside the first man. Minor: one tiny far-left background figure (about x 0.02, y 0.4) wears a dark coat, but he is barely readable at print size. The plain white pennant has no text. No text, gore or anachronism of note. Lettering space for the three captions: the open night sky from x 0.5 to 0.85 across the top fifth, plus the sand between the fire groups at bottom centre.

v01 fails: the ear has a hanging gold drop. v02 (ear region edit) passes: a small round gold stud sits on the lobe with nothing hanging. Seen enlarged, it looks slightly ring-like, but at print size it is a small gold dot. In this back view the moustache tip shows and the jaw is in shadow, with no beard. Boots, sleeves down, talwar, and the turban tail blowing in the wind all match the script. He stands on a rocky rise seen from behind, above a black sea with no ships, with campfires and tents at the left. Minor: some fires at the camp edge throw up heavy smoke, but it reads as cookfires, not a burning camp. No text or anachronism. The whole upper right is empty night sky for the caption.

Clean on every hard check. It shows a Carnatic tent (not Kerala). The captive is heavy and bearded, in a soiled white jama and a high cream turban with no jewel, his face in profile shadow, iron manacles and chain at his wrists. Maratha officers in white angarkhas and white or saffron pagdis, with saffron or brown sashes (no red), count coin on a white cloth. A saffron swallow-tailed pennant hangs at the tent door. The hanging lamp is a pierced brass lantern, which suits a Carnatic tent. There is no text. Minor points: the vision is drawn as an ordinary tent interior, not 'bleeding across the night sky above the sea' (a soft edge or vignette can be added when compositing). The two silhouetted guards at the door wear dark, checked clothing rather than white angarkhas. The dark tent canopy at top centre, roughly x 0.27 to 0.70 and y 0 to 0.27, is clear space for both captions.

All hard checks pass. The ear ornament is a tiny gold stud flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. The chin is clean-shaven (only light ink hatching on the jaw, which reads clean at size). The thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash all match. Campfire smoke drifts across his face in the sea wind, and his expression is serious and certain, not triumphant. There is no text. Minor point: the small background figures at the left-edge fire wear dark caps and dark tunics with crossbelts, not the Nair and Deccan dress of 8.1. They are tiny, half-hidden in smoke, and away from the lettering. The night sky at top right, roughly x 0.55 to 1.0 and y 0 to 0.30, holds both captions clear of the face.

v01 fails: the ear has a hanging gold drop. v02 (ear region edit) passes: a tiny gold stud sits flush on the lobe, the chin is clean-shaven with a thick curled moustache, sleeves are down, and he wears boots and a talwar. Full-width night shot: Nagoji has turned from the sea and walks along the rise past the camp fires, while the long pale empty beach and the moonlit sea run away to the right, as scripted. Minor: the background camp figures wear turbans and tunics rather than the bare-headed Nairs of 8.1 (they could pass for Deccan riders), and Nagoji walks toward the viewer past the fires rather than straight into them. No text, gore or anachronism. Ample dark sky from x 0.35 to 0.85 across the top third for the caption.
